{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01ALa4xwCahY53UnZB6v2VR9","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Nth Technologies, Inc. — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-14\n     4→Developer website: https://www.nablemd.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Nth Technologies, Inc. is a small health IT company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Houston, Texas (12 Greenway Plaza, Suite 1100). The company has 11–50 employees and was founded after the founder's wife encountered difficulties managing a small Ob/Gyn practice, which motivated building an integrated EMR/PM solution. The company develops and sells nAbleMD, a cloud-based EHR and practice management platform, and nAble IVF, a specialized fertility clinic management system. Both operate under the \"nAble\" brand.\n     9→\n    10→Nth Technologies positions itself as serving small to medium-sized ambulatory practices across multiple specialties. The company has a notable concentration in fertility/IVF clinics, where it reports 200+ providers, 1 million+ completed cycles, and $800M+ in payments processed. The general nAbleMD product serves a broader range of specialties. The company operates with no long-term contracts and inclusive pricing (no fees for upgrades, support, data migration, or configuration). The contact for certification matters is Fredrick Knieper (fknieper@nthtechnology.com).\n    11→\n    12→## Product: nAbleMD\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11118 (version 6.0c, certified 2022-12-21)\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→nAbleMD is a cloud-based, integrated electronic medical records (EMR) and practice management (PM) platform designed for ambulatory practices. It was \"designed from the ground up as a web-based system\" and includes native mobile apps for iPad and Android tablets, plus iPhone and Android patient portal apps. The certified product encompasses both the clinical EMR and the practice management/billing modules as a single integrated platform.\n    19→\n    20→The product is certified for 38 ONC criteria spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)–(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(4), public health reporting (f)(1), FHIR R4 APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10), and Direct messaging (h)(1). This is a broad certification footprint indicating a full-featured ambulatory EHR.\n    21→\n    22→### Users & Market\n    23→\n    24→nAbleMD targets small to medium-sized ambulatory practices. The vendor's website and third-party listings indicate support for the following specialties through specialty-specific modules:\n    25→\n    26→- **Fertility/IVF** (primary specialty focus — separate nAble IVF product with dedicated website)\n    27→- **Obstetrics & Gynecology**\n    28→- **Family Medicine**\n    29→- **Internal Medicine**\n    30→- **Pediatrics**\n    31→- **Cardiology**\n    32→- **Gastroenterology**\n    33→- **ENT (Otolaryngology)**\n    34→- **Urology**\n    35→- **General Surgery**\n    36→- **Urgent Care**\n    37→- **Behavioral Health**\n    38→\n    39→Each specialty gets customized templates, picklists, and workflows. Named customers include Houston Fertility Institute, Memorial OB-GYN, Bloom Fertility (INVO Fertility), Palm Beach Fertility, Tree of Life Fertility, Idaho Fertility Center, and Fertility Treatment Services — skewing heavily toward fertility and Ob/Gyn practices. The IVF-specific product reports 200+ providers; the total nAbleMD user base across all specialties is not publicly disclosed but appears modest given the small company size.\n    40→\n    41→User reviews are sparse. SelectHub gives it a 96% user satisfaction rating based on 8 reviews. Capterra lists it but had no accessible reviews. Users highlight the integrated design and customer support as strengths; the patient portal has been criticized as less intuitive than expected.\n    42→\n    43→### Modules & Functionality\n    44→\n    45→Based on vendor materials (nablemd.com, nablesupport.com, nableivf.com) and third-party listings:\n    46→\n    47→**Clinical EMR:**\n    48→- Patient charting and clinical documentation with specialty-specific templates\n    49→- HPI (History of Present Illness) templates\n    50→- Physical exam diagrams with annotation and color markers\n    51→- Medication and allergy documentation with interaction alerts\n    52→- e-Prescribing (integrated with NewCrop/Surescripts)\n    53→- Lab ordering and results management (LabCorp interface mentioned specifically)\n    54→- Radiology and 64→- Patient check-in (including iPad kiosk)\n    65→- Eligibility verification\n    66→- ICD-10 coding\n    67→- Charge capture with E&M codes\n    68→- Automated claims submission (clearinghouse   89→- Secure intra-office messaging\n    90→- Transitions of care (C-CDA) document exchange\n    91→\n    92→**IVF/Fertility-Specific Features** (via nAble IVF module/product):\n    93→- Interactive cycle management with treatment plans and stimulation protocols\n    94→- Oocyte tracking from retrieval through embryo transfer\n    95→- Semen analysis documentation\n    96→- Cryostorage management **Consent forms** — digital consent management (especially IVF)\n   138→- **Clinical quality measure data** — certified (c)(1)–(c)(4), 13 CQM measure sets\n   139→- **Public health reporting data** — certified (f)(1) immunization reporting\n   140→- **Transitions of care documents** — C-CDA, certified (b)(1)–(b)(3)\n   141→- **Audit logs** — certified (d)(2)\n   142→\n   143→For IVF practices **Cryostorage inventory** — frozen specimens (sperm, eggs, embryos), tank/cylinder/cane locations, barcode data\n   147→- **Semen analysis results**\n   148→- **Donor records and evaluations**\n   149→- **SART reporting data**\n   150→\n   151→The mandatory disclosures page notes that \"images and non-standard documentation require separate one-time fees for bulk export,\" which suggests that nAbleMD and nAble IVF appear to share the same underlying platform (the IVF app connects to \"nAbleMD's database\" per the App Store listing) but are marketed as distinct products. The IVF product has its own dedicated website (nableivf.com) and appears to be the vendor's strongest market position.\n   158→- The company is small (11–50 employees) and appears to be a niche vendor. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KaZZ9cfygFfP8cJvyHYRFx","type":"tool_result","content":"    <a href=\"cert_cure/Compliance%20Certificate%20nAbleMD%206.0c%20122324.pdf\" title=\"Click to View Certification Details\"><input type=\"button\" value=\"Click to View Certificate\"></a>\n    </center>\n    <br><br>\n          <h2>Costs and Requirements:</h2>\n          Use of this certified product-version requires a contract with an ongoing monthly subscription fee which is charged per top-level provider (minimum one per practice).  This subscription fee includes access to the software, patient portal, support, and any updates to the software.   The fee also includes access for this provided to the electronic prescription system (see below).   Training and transportation fees apply for in-person or dedicated online training sessions.  An internet connection is required for all access to the software.<br><br>    \n          For clinics that are discontinuing active use of our software, a reduced monthly fee is available for maintenance of an inactive practice, permitting users to continue accessing existing records without the ability to create any new charts, encounters, prescriptions, or other new records.   While this product-version is certified for Data Portability to generate a set of export summaries of all patients; photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries.   A one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation.  Use of the Data Portability export to create summaries is limited to one active export at a time.  Exporting large numbers of patients may take several hours.<br><br>\n          Electronic Prescribing, Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking are provided by an integrated third party service provided by NewCrop.  First-time users of the service will be automatically prompted to complete an online agreement with NewCrop.   Mid-level providers must pay a monthly fee for access to the integrated prescription service to compose prescriptions, whether transmitted electronically or not.   All staff members may access the Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking without charge.   All prescribers wishing to electronically prescribe controlled substances must pay an annual identity certification fee per prescriber in addition to a monthly charge per prescriber.  Electronic prescription of medical marijuana is not possible at this time.<br><br>\n          Access to the Surescripts Direct Messaging network is provided via the NewCrop prescription service and requires an additional monthly fee per address, which is tied to a single prescribing provider.  Use of this network is required for updating the patients' Medication List and Allergy List by reconciling medications and allergies received in documentation from other providers.    Integration of alternate HISPs is not available.    Sending and receiving Direct messages with a provider using a different network requires a trust relationship between Surescripts and the other provider's network.  In the event that a trust relationship does not exist, Nth Technologies will submit a request to Surescripts to establish one.<br><br>\n          Additional one-time charges may apply for establishing radiology or laboratory interfaces to incorporate laboratory test results and radiology/imaging results into the chart.  These charges are typically paid by the laboratory or imaging service and cover the development and testing of the interface.  In the event that the laboratory or imaging center is not willing to pay for the interface, the clinic will be responsible for this charge.  For laboratory or imaging equipment such as ultrasound machines used in the practice, the ability to establish direct interfaces with the equipment may be limited, even if the device has internet access.  Interfaces with these devices are handled on a case-by-case basis.<br><br>\n          Interfaces for automated submission of immunizations to immunization registries do not yet exist for all states.  These interfaces are developed on an on-demand basis and are made available at no charge to customers once completed.  Customers in a state without automatic submission will be required to manually submit immunization record data files following their registry's instructions until an automated interface is completed.   Interfaces with Syndromic Surveillance registries are also developed on an on-demand basis at no charge to the customer.  Both kinds of on-demand interfaces may take several weeks to be completed, depending on the complexity of the interface and the number of interfaces requested across all customers.<br><br>\n\n\t  <h2>Multi-Factor Authentication</h2>\n\t  nAbleMD has Multi-Factor Authentication available as an option to improve security of the application.  Utilizing this requires a token or application capable of storing a secret key (either alphanumeric or QR graphic) and generating a Time-based One Time Password (TOTP) code.  When a user activates the feature, after entering their username and password they will need to enter the one-time password generated by the token or application to complete the login process.\n\n\t  <h2>API Documentation</h2>\n\t  API Documentation and terms of use are available at the following locations:\n\t  <ul>\n\t\t  <li><a href=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/index.html\">FHIR 4.0.1 API Documentation</a></li>\n\t\t  <li><a href=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/terms_and_conditions.html\">API Terms and Conditions of Use</a>\n\t  </ul>\n\n          <h2>Electronic Health Information Export</h2>\n          Documentation for the patient Electronic Health Information (EHI) export can be found here:\n          <ul>\n                  <li><a href=\"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11Yj6cH8GsXPnTuxDDIvYwgoF5sgM6zrwy4Ql6OEdWRQ/edit?gid=1058514257#gid=1058514257\">nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary</a></li>\n          </ul>\n\n\t  <h2>Real World Testing</h2>\n\t  Real World Testing is intended to show that certain certified features of the software function properly in clincal settings when used by providers.  This table contains our Real World Test plans and documentation of the results:\n          <table>\n          <thead><tr><th style=\"vertical-align:top;padding:0 1em;\">Year</th><th style=\"vertical-align:top;padding:0 1em;\">Documentation</th></tr></thead>\n          <tbody>\n\t\t  <tr><td style=\"vertical-align:top;padding: 0.5em 1em;\">2022</td><td {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MiTAxE1D5P1tdrR4LWRD64","type":"tool_result","content":"\"Export Creation Process\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"1. Authorization to perform export:\n\nTo authorize a user to perform an export, the administrator must  give the user access to the Data Export screen under System Configuration.  The user must also enable 2FA protection on their account by accessing PM Home -> Settiings -> Preferences -> My Account and following the prompts at the bottom to Enable 2-Factor Authentication.\n\n2. Performing an export of a single patient's record\n\nAn authorized user can perform the export of a single patient's record by accessing the PM Home -> System Configuration -> Data Export screen.  Here, click the magnifying glass to open the patient search.  Select a patient, then press the \"\"Request Download\"\" button.  A password prompt will appear, you must enter a password to encrypt the zip file in order to initiate the process.  The pending epxort will appear in the Data Export list as pending.  An export of a single patient's record can be expected to take approximately 5 minutes, though patients with a large number of ultrasound images or other documents may take longer.\n\n3. Performing a complete export of all records\n\nAn authorized user can export all records in the software by accessing the PM Home -> System Configuration -> Data Export screen.  Here, press the \"\"Request Download\"\" button without selecting a patient. A password prompt will appear, you must enter a password to encrypt the zip file in order to initiate the process.  Note that the duration of this process will depend on the total number of patients and the amount of stored images or documents.\n\n4. Retrieving the completed export\n\nOnce complete the export file(s) will be shown with checksums and download links for each one. Please use the browser's refresh button to screen to check the export progress.  You may also leave the screen and return later.   Each zip volume is approximately 10GB of data.  Export files will be retained on the server for 7 days.\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"Documentation For .zip format \",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"The zip format is a compressed arrchive file format created by the 7-zip open-source file archiver.   It utilizes AES-256 encryption to secure the medical records.  Note that some versions of windows will indicate that this file is corrupt due to lack of support for this level of encryption.  Use of a third-party archive tool is required to open and extract these archives.  We recommend the freely available 7-zip utility which is available from https://www.7-zip.org/download \n\nWhen initiating the export, a password must be given to encrypt the archive.  This password must be used in order to extract data files from the archive and cannot be recovered if it is lost or forgotten.  Please make sure to store the password in a safe place such as a secure password safe.  We strongly recommend not storing the archive and password in the same location, especially on a removable thumbdrive or disk, as in the event the drive is stolen, the password can then be used to extract the data.\n\n➡️ You can extract the the data by opening the *filename*.zip.001 file.  Note that if multiple volumes are created (.zip.001, .zip.002, etc), all volumes must be stored in a single folder.  Opening the first volume (001) will open all following volumes as necessary, you do not need to individually open each volume.\n➡️ Enter the password that you selected while exporting the data\n➡️ Drag and drop files from the archive to another location to extract them.\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"Documentation For .csv format\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"CSV is a simple and widely used file format for storing tablular data. In a CSV file, each line of the file represents a record of data separated by a newline character, and the cells (fields) in each row are reparated by commas.  The first row of each file is the heading, each comma-separated value indicating the title of that column.  String data should be expected to be encoded in UTF-8.\n\nColumns without data will simply be empty.  Note that there is no distinction between an empty string and a \"\"NULL\"\" value in this case.  Strings that contain newlines, double quotation marks (\"\") and will themselves be enclosed in doulbe quotation marks.  Double quotation marks occurring within a string will be doubled (\"\"\"\")\n\nExample for a data table of a person's name, age and hometown, containing 3 records.  The first record, the name field contains a comma and is therefore enclosed in quotes.  The second record has a name containing quotes, and is therefore enclosed in quotes and the quotes within the string are doubled.  The third record contains a person with no hometown.\n\nName,Age,Hometown\n\"\"Hancock, John\"\",39,Houston\n\"\"John \"\"\"\"The Don\"\"\"\" Doe\"\",52,Chicago\nSusie Wanderer,38,\n\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"Document Repository\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"Scanned documents, DICOM files, HL7 messages, and various other artefacts are stored in the Document Repository rather than the CSV files.  The Documents CSV file contains a column with the filename to the document relative to the Documents folder within the archive..  The file extension should generally reflect the content type.however a Mime-type column is present in the Documents table when the mime-type of the document is known.  Please note that the format of any given type of file stored in the repository is outside of the scope of this documentation.\n\nDocumentrs and images: These files generally end in .pdf, .png, .jpg, .gif, .tif, however as any document may be uploaded to nAbleMD it may also include .doc, .docx, and other document formats.\nANSI Claim/EDI messages: These files generally end in .835, .837, .277, .277FE, .271, .271.xml (for XML-wrapped 271 files used by some clearinghouses).  There may be other non-standard claim message files such as .DPR or .EBR\nHL7 messages: Generally end in .hl7.  Typically .orm.hl7 for laboratory test result files and .oru.hl7 for laboratory test order files.  Imaging/Radiology orders may also use this format.\nDICOM: Generally end in .dcm.  Note that files may be either image data or Structured Report (SR) data, as transmitted by the interfaced machines.\n\nNote that within nAble there may be documents stored in the Docment Archive that are not associated wiht any patient, such as incoming faxes that have not been filed to a chart or documents intentionally uploaded outside of a patient chart.  These documents will only be exported when a full export is requested.\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"This Guide\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"This guide contains documentation and data dictionary for the CSV files exported from nAbleMD 6.0c.  Please see the Revision History tab for more details.\n\nThe Table of Contents tab lists the various data tables that are exported and included in the archive.  Note that not all data tables are used by all specialties, please check the specialty column of the Table of Contents to see if a particular data table is relevant to your practice,  After the Table of Contents tab is a tab containing a description of each data table and the columns as exported to the CSV file. The name of the tab matches the name of the CSV file (plus the \"\".csv\"\" extension) thus the \"\"Visit.csv\"\" file is documented in the Visit tab.\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3a2a27aa-0d8e-4d83-820c-9d922f391773","uuid":"d3a5bbf2-0c90-445c-b93e-4fd43966bbbe","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"Export Creation Process\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\",\"\"\n\"1. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_016hX7pKBoTfMqthGSnQRyK4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011aNQaqqYuXTnYDtacEAFED","name":"mcp__plugin_chrome-devtools-mcp_chrome-devtools__evaluate_script","input":{"function":"() => {\n  // Try to extract GIDs by clicking each tab and noting the URL change\n  // First, let's check the page source for gid mappings\n  const html = document.documentElement.innerHTML;\n  // Look for patterns like \"gid\":NUMBER\n  const gidMatches = html.match(/\"gid\"\\s*:\\s*(\\d+)/g);\n  if (gidMatches) {\n    return gidMatches.slice(0, 200);\n  }\n  \n  // Also try to find sheet data in the bootstrapData\n  const scripts = document.querySelectorAll('script');\n  for (const s of scripts) {\n    if (s.textContent.includes('sheetId')) {\n      return s.textContent.substring(0, 2000);\n    }\n  }\n  \n  return 'No gid data found in page source';\n}"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":101,"cache_read_input_tokens":59972,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":101},"output_tokens":38,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3a2a27aa-0d8e-4d83-820c-9d922f391773","uuid":"8645752f-e2d5-4edd-89a9-e9d16187a807"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01Pw4BTZzjtMCZhfgTNgUvEq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01X7FMZjhd5i9VUXszep1jHu","name":"mcp__plugin_chrome-devtools-mcp_chrome-devtools__evaluate_script","input":{"function":"async () => {\n  // Get GIDs by clicking each tab and reading the URL hash\n  const tabs = document.querySelectorAll('.docs-sheet-tab');\n  const results = [];\n  \n  for (let i = 0; i < tabs.length; i++) {\n    const tab = tabs[i];\n    const name = tab.querySelector('.docs-sheet-tab-name')?.textContent;\n    tab.click();\n    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100));\n    const hash = window.location.hash;\n    const gidMatch = hash.match(/gid=(\\d+)/);\n    const gid = gidMatch ? gidMatch[1] : null;\n    results.push({ name: name?.trim(), gid });\n  }\n  \n  return results;\n}"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":321,"cache_read_input_tokens":60073,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":321},"output_tokens":38,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3a2a27aa-0d8e-4d83-820c-9d922f391773","uuid":"a8e15fed-51fb-4a12-bed4-d39b69f17de0"}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RLFg2hidw5i6WKYnv2TtMx","type":"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# take_snapshot response\n## Latest page snapshot\nuid=1_0 RootWebArea \"nAble\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\"\n  uid=1_1 navigation\n    uid=1_2 button \"Login\"\n    uid=1_3 link \"nable\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/index.html\"\n      uid=1_4 image \"nable\" description=\"nable\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/img/logo.png\"\n    uid=1_5 link \"Practice Solutions\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/practice-solution.html\"\n      uid=1_6 StaticText \"Practice\"\n      uid=1_7 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_8 StaticText \"Solutions\"\n    uid=1_9 link \"New! IVF Solutions\" url=\"http://www.nableivf.com/\"\n      uid=1_10 StaticText \"New! IVF\"\n      uid=1_11 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_12 StaticText \"Solutions\"\n    uid=1_13 link \"Mobile Apps\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/mobile-apps.html\"\n      uid=1_14 StaticText \"Mobile\"\n      uid=1_15 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_16 StaticText \"Apps\"\n    uid=1_17 link \"Pricing Plans\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_18 StaticText \"Pricing\"\n      uid=1_19 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_20 StaticText \"Plans\"\n    uid=1_21 link \"About Us\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_22 StaticText \"About\"\n      uid=1_23 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_24 StaticText \"Us\"\n    uid=1_25 link \"Contact Us\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_26 StaticText \"Contact\"\n      uid=1_27 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_28 StaticText \"Us\"\n  uid=1_29 main\n    uid=1_30 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_31 StaticText \"This Health IT Module is compliant with the ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. This certification does not represent an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.\"\n    uid=1_32 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_33 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_34 StaticText \"Vendor Name:\"\n    uid=1_35 StaticText \" Nth Technologies\"\n    uid=1_36 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_37 StaticText \"Date Certified:\"\n    uid=1_38 StaticText \" 12/21/2022\"\n    uid=1_39 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_40 StaticText \"Product Version:\"\n    uid=1_41 StaticText \" 6.0c\"\n    uid=1_42 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_43 StaticText \"Certification ID Number:\"\n    uid=1_44 StaticText \" 15.04.04.2070.nAbl.06.01.1.221221\"\n    uid=1_45 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_46 StaticText \"Criteria Tested:\"\n    uid=1_47 StaticText \" 170.315 (a)(1-5, 12, 14); (b)(1-3, 7-11); (c)(1-4); (d)(1-9, 12-13); (e)(1, 3); (f)(1, 7); (g)(2-7, 9-10); (h)(1)\"\n    uid=1_48 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_49 StaticText \"Clinical Quality Measures Certified:\"\n    uid=1_50 StaticText \" 22v6; 68v7; 69v6; 75v6; 117v6; 122v6; 125v6; 138v6; 146v6; 147v7; 155v6; 165v6; 166v7\"\n    uid=1_51 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_52 StaticText \"Additional Software Used:\"\n    uid=1_53 StaticText \" NLM AccessGUDI API, Surescripts Clinical Direct Messaging, NewCropRx\"\n    uid=1_54 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_55 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_56 link \"Click to View Certificate\" description=\"Click to View Certification Details\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/cert_cure/Compliance%20Certificate%20nAbleMD%206.0c%20122324.pdf\"\n      uid=1_57 button \"Click to View Certificate\"\n    uid=1_58 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_59 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_60 heading \"Costs and Requirements:\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_61 StaticText \"Use of this certified product-version requires a contract with an ongoing monthly subscription fee which is charged per top-level provider (minimum one per practice). This subscription fee includes access to the software, patient portal, support, and any updates to the software. The fee also includes access for this provided to the electronic prescription system (see below). Training and transportation fees apply for in-person or dedicated online training sessions. An internet connection is required for all access to the software.\"\n    uid=1_62 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_63 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_64 StaticText \"For clinics that are discontinuing active use of our software, a reduced monthly fee is available for maintenance of an inactive practice, permitting users to continue accessing existing records without the ability to create any new charts, encounters, prescriptions, or other new records. While this product-version is certified for Data Portability to generate a set of export summaries of all patients; photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries. A one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation. Use of the Data Portability export to create summaries is limited to one active export at a time. Exporting large numbers of patients may take several hours.\"\n    uid=1_65 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_66 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_67 StaticText \"Electronic Prescribing, Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking are provided by an integrated third party service provided by NewCrop. First-time users of the service will be automatically prompted to complete an online agreement with NewCrop. Mid-level providers must pay a monthly fee for access to the integrated prescription service to compose prescriptions, whether transmitted electronically or not. All staff members may access the Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking without charge. All prescribers wishing to electronically prescribe controlled substances must pay an annual identity certification fee per prescriber in addition to a monthly charge per prescriber. Electronic prescription of medical marijuana is not possible at this time.\"\n    uid=1_68 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_69 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_70 StaticText \"Access to the Surescripts Direct Messaging network is provided via the NewCrop prescription service and requires an additional monthly fee per address, which is tied to a single prescribing provider. Use of this network is required for updating the patients' Medication List and Allergy List by reconciling medications and allergies received in documentation from other providers. Integration of alternate HISPs is not available. Sending and receiving Direct messages with a provider using a different network requires a trust relationship between Surescripts and the other provider's network. In the event that a trust relationship does not exist, Nth Technologies will submit a request to Surescripts to establish one.\"\n    uid=1_71 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_72 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_73 StaticText \"Additional one-time charges may apply for establishing radiology or laboratory interfaces to incorporate laboratory test results and radiology/imaging results into the chart. These charges are typically paid by the laboratory or imaging service and cover the development and testing of the interface. In the event that the laboratory or imaging center is not willing to pay for the interface, the clinic will be responsible for this charge. For laboratory or imaging equipment such as ultrasound machines used in the practice, the ability to establish direct interfaces with the equipment may be limited, even if the device has internet access. Interfaces with these devices are handled on a case-by-case basis.\"\n    uid=1_74 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_75 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_76 StaticText \"Interfaces for automated submission of immunizations to immunization registries do not yet exist for all states. These interfaces are developed on an on-demand basis and are made available at no charge to customers once completed. Customers in a state without automatic submission will be required to manually submit immunization record data files following their registry's instructions until an automated interface is completed. Interfaces with Syndromic Surveillance registries are also developed on an on-demand basis at no charge to the customer. Both kinds of on-demand interfaces may take several weeks to be completed, depending on the complexity of the interface and the number of interfaces requested across all customers.\"\n    uid=1_77 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_78 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_79 heading \"Multi-Factor Authentication\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_80 StaticText \"nAbleMD has Multi-Factor Authentication available as an option to improve security of the application. Utilizing this requires a token or application capable of storing a secret key (either alphanumeric or QR graphic) and generating a Time-based One Time Password (TOTP) code. When a user activates the feature, after entering their username and password they will need to enter the one-time password generated by the token or application to complete the login process.\"\n    uid=1_81 heading \"API Documentation\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_82 StaticText \"API Documentation and terms of use are available at the following locations:\"\n    uid=1_83 link \"FHIR 4.0.1 API Documentation\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/index.html\"\n      uid=1_84 StaticText \"FHIR 4.0.1 API Documentation\"\n    uid=1_85 link \"API Terms and Conditions of Use\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/terms_and_conditions.html\"\n      uid=1_86 StaticText \"API Terms and Conditions of Use\"\n    uid=1_87 heading \"Electronic Health Information Export\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_88 StaticText \"Documentation for the patient Electronic Health Information (EHI) export can be found here:\"\n    uid=1_89 link \"nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary\" url=\"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11Yj6cH8GsXPnTuxDDIvYwgoF5sgM6zrwy4Ql6OEdWRQ/edit?gid=1058514257#gid=1058514257\"\n      uid=1_90 StaticText \"nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary\"\n    uid=1_91 heading \"Real World Testing\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_92 StaticText \"Real World Testing is intended to show that certain certified features of the software function properly in clincal settings when used by providers. This table contains our Real World Test plans and documentation of the results:\"\n    uid=1_93 StaticText \"Year\"\n    uid=1_94 StaticText \"Documentation\"\n    uid=1_95 StaticText \"2022\"\n IVF Solutions\" url=\"http://www.nableivf.com/\"\n      uid=1_10 StaticText \"New! IVF\"\n      uid=1_11 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_12 StaticText \"Solutions\"\n    uid=1_13 link \"Mobile Apps\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/mobile-apps.html\"\n      uid=1_14 StaticText \"Mobile\"\n      uid=1_15 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_16 StaticText \"Apps\"\n    uid=1_17 link \"Pricing Plans\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_18 StaticText \"Pricing\"\n      uid=1_19 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_20 StaticText \"Plans\"\n    uid=1_21 link \"About Us\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_22 StaticText \"About\"\n      uid=1_23 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_24 StaticText \"Us\"\n    uid=1_25 link \"Contact Us\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html#\"\n      uid=1_26 StaticText \"Contact\"\n      uid=1_27 LineBreak \"\n\"\n      uid=1_28 StaticText \"Us\"\n  uid=1_29 main\n    uid=1_30 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_31 StaticText \"This Health IT Module is compliant with the ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. This certification does not represent an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.\"\n    uid=1_32 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_33 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_34 StaticText \"Vendor Name:\"\n    uid=1_35 StaticText \" Nth Technologies\"\n    uid=1_36 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_37 StaticText \"Date Certified:\"\n    uid=1_38 StaticText \" 12/21/2022\"\n    uid=1_39 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_40 StaticText \"Product Version:\"\n    uid=1_41 StaticText \" 6.0c\"\n    uid=1_42 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_43 StaticText \"Certification ID Number:\"\n    uid=1_44 StaticText \" 15.04.04.2070.nAbl.06.01.1.221221\"\n    uid=1_45 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_46 StaticText \"Criteria Tested:\"\n    uid=1_47 StaticText \" 170.315 (a)(1-5, 12, 14); (b)(1-3, 7-11); (c)(1-4); (d)(1-9, 12-13); (e)(1, 3); (f)(1, 7); (g)(2-7, 9-10); (h)(1)\"\n    uid=1_48 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_49 StaticText \"Clinical Quality Measures Certified:\"\n    uid=1_50 StaticText \" 22v6; 68v7; 69v6; 75v6; 117v6; 122v6; 125v6; 138v6; 146v6; 147v7; 155v6; 165v6; 166v7\"\n    uid=1_51 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_52 StaticText \"Additional Software Used:\"\n    uid=1_53 StaticText \" NLM AccessGUDI API, Surescripts Clinical Direct Messaging, NewCropRx\"\n    uid=1_54 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_55 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_56 link \"Click to View Certificate\" description=\"Click to View Certification Details\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/cert_cure/Compliance%20Certificate%20nAbleMD%206.0c%20122324.pdf\"\n      uid=1_57 button \"Click to View Certificate\"\n    uid=1_58 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_59 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_60 heading \"Costs and Requirements:\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_61 StaticText \"Use of this certified product-version requires a contract with an ongoing monthly subscription fee which is charged per top-level provider (minimum one per practice). This subscription fee includes access to the software, patient portal, support, and any updates to the software. The fee also includes access for this provided to the electronic prescription system (see below). Training and transportation fees apply for in-person or dedicated online training sessions. An internet connection is required for all access to the software.\"\n    uid=1_62 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_63 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_64 StaticText \"For clinics that are discontinuing active use of our software, a reduced monthly fee is available for maintenance of an inactive practice, permitting users to continue accessing existing records without the ability to create any new charts, encounters, prescriptions, or other new records. While this product-version is certified for Data Portability to generate a set of export summaries of all patients; photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries. A one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation. Use of the Data Portability export to create summaries is limited to one active export at a time. Exporting large numbers of patients may take several hours.\"\n    uid=1_65 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_66 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_67 StaticText \"Electronic Prescribing, Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking are provided by an integrated third party service provided by NewCrop. First-time users of the service will be automatically prompted to complete an online agreement with NewCrop. Mid-level providers must pay a monthly fee for access to the integrated prescription service to compose prescriptions, whether transmitted electronically or not. All staff members may access the Drug Formulary and Drug-drug/Drug-allergy interaction checking without charge. All prescribers wishing to electronically prescribe controlled substances must pay an annual identity certification fee per prescriber in addition to a monthly charge per prescriber. Electronic prescription of medical marijuana is not possible at this time.\"\n    uid=1_68 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_69 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_70 StaticText \"Access to the Surescripts Direct Messaging network is provided via the NewCrop prescription service and requires an additional monthly fee per address, which is tied to a single prescribing provider. Use of this network is required for updating the patients' Medication List and Allergy List by reconciling medications and allergies received in documentation from other providers. Integration of alternate HISPs is not available. Sending and receiving Direct messages with a provider using a different network requires a trust relationship between Surescripts and the other provider's network. In the event that a trust relationship does not exist, Nth Technologies will submit a request to Surescripts to establish one.\"\n    uid=1_71 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_72 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_73 StaticText \"Additional one-time charges may apply for establishing radiology or laboratory interfaces to incorporate laboratory test results and radiology/imaging results into the chart. These charges are typically paid by the laboratory or imaging service and cover the development and testing of the interface. In the event that the laboratory or imaging center is not willing to pay for the interface, the clinic will be responsible for this charge. For laboratory or imaging equipment such as ultrasound machines used in the practice, the ability to establish direct interfaces with the equipment may be limited, even if the device has internet access. Interfaces with these devices are handled on a case-by-case basis.\"\n    uid=1_74 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_75 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_76 StaticText \"Interfaces for automated submission of immunizations to immunization registries do not yet exist for all states. These interfaces are developed on an on-demand basis and are made available at no charge to customers once completed. Customers in a state without automatic submission will be required to manually submit immunization record data files following their registry's instructions until an automated interface is completed. Interfaces with Syndromic Surveillance registries are also developed on an on-demand basis at no charge to the customer. Both kinds of on-demand interfaces may take several weeks to be completed, depending on the complexity of the interface and the number of interfaces requested across all customers.\"\n    uid=1_77 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_78 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_79 heading \"Multi-Factor Authentication\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_80 StaticText \"nAbleMD has Multi-Factor Authentication available as an option to improve security of the application. Utilizing this requires a token or application capable of storing a secret key (either alphanumeric or QR graphic) and generating a Time-based One Time Password (TOTP) code. When a user activates the feature, after entering their username and password they will need to enter the one-time password generated by the token or application to complete the login process.\"\n    uid=1_81 heading \"API Documentation\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_82 StaticText \"API Documentation and terms of use are available at the following locations:\"\n    uid=1_83 link \"FHIR 4.0.1 API Documentation\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/index.html\"\n      uid=1_84 StaticText \"FHIR 4.0.1 API Documentation\"\n    uid=1_85 link \"API Terms and Conditions of Use\" url=\"https://www.nablemd.com/api_fhir/terms_and_conditions.html\"\n      uid=1_86 StaticText \"API Terms and Conditions of Use\"\n    uid=1_87 heading \"Electronic Health Information Export\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_88 StaticText \"Documentation for the patient Electronic Health Information (EHI) export can be found here:\"\n    uid=1_89 link \"nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary\" url=\"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11Yj6cH8GsXPnTuxDDIvYwgoF5sgM6zrwy4Ql6OEdWRQ/edit?gid=1058514257#gid=1058514257\"\n      uid=1_90 StaticText \"nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary\"\n    uid=1_91 heading \"Real World Testing\" level=\"2\"\n    uid=1_92 StaticText \"Real World Testing is intended to show that certain certified features of the software function properly in clincal settings when used by providers. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01PDChPyiGiAtCsDv1xMuq6E","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TPLcoVghH3iVJ2drnxctoy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/nth-technologies-inc/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Nth Technologies, Inc. — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-14\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\n- CHPL IDs: 11118\n- Product: nAbleMD 6.0c\n- Certification date: 2022-12-21\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe:**\n   ```bash\n   curl -sI -L \"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html, 36,088 bytes. No redirects.\n\n2. **Downloaded and examined the page:**\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o certification-page.html\n   ```\n   The page is a standard compliance/mandatory disclosures page with sections for: certification details, costs and requirements, MFA, API documentation, **Electronic Health Information Export**, and Real World Testing.\n\n3. **Found the EHI Export section** — a dedicated `<h2>` heading \"Electronic Health Information Export\" near the bottom of the page, containing a single link:\n   - [nAbleMD 6.0c export guide and data dictionary](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11Yj6cH8GsXPnTuxDDIvYwgoF5sgM6zrwy4Ql6OEdWRQ/edit?gid=1058514257#gid=1058514257)\n\n4. **Examined the Google Sheets data dictionary.** The spreadsheet is publicly accessible (view-only). It has the title \"CSV Export Format Documentation - External\" and contains 109 tabs:\n   - \"Read Me\" — export creation process, documentation for .zip format, .csv format, document repository, and guide overview\n   - \"Revision History\" — version tracking (v1.0 11/30/2023, v1.0.1 12/12/2023)\n   - \"Table of Contents\" — index of ~107 data tables\n   - 106 individual data table tabs, each documenting one CSV export file with FieldName and Description columns\n\n5. **Downloaded all 109 sheets as CSV** using the Google Sheets gviz/tq endpoint:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11Yj6cH8GsXPnTuxDDIvYwgoF5sgM6zrwy4Ql6OEdWRQ/gviz/tq?tqx=out:csv&gid=GID\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o FILENAME.csv\n   ```\n   All 109 files verified as valid CSV (not HTML error pages). The direct XLSX export endpoint returned HTML auth walls, so per-sheet CSV via the gviz endpoint was used instead.\n\n6. **Noted important context from the \"Costs and Requirements\" section** on the certification page:\n   > \"While this product-version is certified for Data Portability to generate a set of export summaries of all patients; photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries. A one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation.\"\n\n   This indicates that the standard export covers structured data, while binary documents/images require a separate fee-based bulk export.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### Export Mechanism\n\nThe nAbleMD EHI export is a **CSV-based bulk export** with an accompanying document repository. The export produces an encrypted 7-zip archive containing:\n\n1. **CSV files** — one per data table (106+ tables), with UTF-8 encoding, comma-separated, first row as headers\n2. **A document repository folder** — containing scanned documents, DICOM files, HL7 messages, faxes, and other attachments referenced by the Document CSV table\n\n### How to Perform the Export\n\nPer the \"Read Me\" tab:\n- **Authorization**: An administrator must grant the user access to the Data Export screen under System Configuration. The user must also enable 2FA on their account.\n- **Single patient export**: PM Home → System Configuration → Data Export → select patient → \"Request Download\" → enter encryption password. Takes ~5 minutes per patient.\n- **Full export**: Same screen, but click \"Request Download\" without selecting a patient. Duration depends on total data volume.\n- **Retrieval**: Completed exports show checksums and download links. Each zip volume is ~10GB. Files retained for 7 days.\n\n### Export Format Details\n\n- **Archive format**: 7-zip with AES-256 encryption, split into ~10GB volumes (.zip.001, .zip.002, etc.)\n- **CSV format**: Standard CSV with UTF-8 encoding. No distinction between empty string and NULL. Strings containing commas, newlines, or quotes are enclosed in double quotes with standard escaping.\n- **Document repository**: Files referenced by the Document table's filename column. Includes:\n  - Documents/images: .pdf, .png, .jpg, .gif, .tif, .doc, .docx\n  - ANSI claim/EDI messages: .835, .837, .277, .277FE, .271, .271.xml, .DPR, .EBR\n  - HL7 messages: .hl7 (.orm.hl7 for results, .oru.hl7 for orders)\n  - DICOM: .dcm (image or Structured Report data)\n\n### Data Dictionary Structure\n\nEach of the 106 data table tabs follows a consistent format:\n- **Table Description** — 1-2 sentences describing the table's purpose and primary key\n- **FieldName / Description** — two-column listing of every exported field with plain-English descriptions\n\nField descriptions include data types implicitly (dates described as \"Date when...\", boolean fields as \"Indicates if/whether...\", foreign keys identified as \"identifier for...\" or \"Map with patientkey\"). No explicit data types, constraints, or value set enumerations are provided, though some descriptions note format details (e.g., \"comma separated if multiple\", gender codes \"M:Male F:Female U:Unknown X:Undifferentiated Blank:Undocumented\").\n\n### Data Tables (106 tables organized by domain)\n\n**Patient Demographics & Registration:**\n- Patients (extensive — ~170 fields covering demographics, addresses, contacts, insurance, fertility-specific fields like blood type, Rh factor, partner info, custom fields 1-10)\n- PatientContact, PatientAllowedContacts, PatientGlobal, PatientNote, Relative, EmrBiologicalFamily\n\n**Clinical Documentation:**\n- ChartNote (chart notes with form content, signatures, cosigning, patient portal release)\n- CosignNote, EmrNotes, EmrEncounterReport, EmrEncounterReportAddendum\n- EmrHpi (History of Present Illness)\n- EmrChiefComplaint\n- EmrReviews (Review of Systems)\n- EmrAssessment\n- EmrPlan\n- EmrChecklistItem\n- EmrAnswerDetail\n\n**Encounters & Visits:**\n- Visit (~75 fields including ICD codes 1-12, claim ID, place of service, provider, charting/approval status)\n- Appointment, AppointmentWaitlist, Action\n\n**Problems, Medications & Allergies:**\n- EmrProblem (diagnoses/problems with ICD codes, onset dates, status)\n- EmrVisitProblem (visit-specific problems)\n- NewcropDrug (medications via NewCrop integration — ~50 fields)\n- NewcropAllergy (allergies via NewCrop)\n- EmrHealthConcern\n- EmrMedicalHistory\n\n**Billing & Financial:**\n- Procedure (CPT/HCPCS codes, modifiers, fees)\n- ProcedureCharge\n- LedgerItem\n- Payment, VisitPayment, PrePayment\n- Insurance (~80 fields — subscriber info, group numbers, authorization details)\n- PriorAuth (prior authorizations)\n- CryoBilling (IVF-specific billing)\n- IvfQuote (IVF treatment quotes)\n\n**Immunizations:**\n- ImmunizationRecord (~35 fields — vaccine codes, lot numbers, manufacturer, VIS dates, administration details)\n- ImmunizationSchedule\n\n**IVF/Fertility-Specific (extensive):**\n- EmrCycle (~200+ fields — comprehensive IVF cycle data)\n- EmrCycleHistory, EmrCycleIntents, EmrCycleDrugPlan, EmrCycleScheduleDay, EmrCycleScheduleRow, EmrCycleScheduleAlert\n- EmrCycleNote, EmrCycleEducation, EmrCycleBirth, EmrCycleCulture\n- EmrOocyte, EmrOocyteDay (oocyte tracking)\n- EmrIvfSample (specimen/sample tracking)\n- EmrIvfSemenAnalysis (~75 fields)\n- EmrIvfFollicularUs (follicular ultrasound)\n- EmrIvfObUs (OB ultrasound)\n- EmrSemenMeasurement\n- EmrDonor (~70 fields), DonorEducation, DonorEmployment, DonorFamily, DonorFamilyDeceased, DonorAnswer\n- EmrDonorPatrequest, CultureMedia\n- EmrInfertilityTreatment, CycleTypeHistory\n- DailyWorklist (embryology daily tasks)\n- EmrContraception\n\n**OB/GYN:**\n- EmrObHistory, EmrObHistoryPreg, EmrObgynhc\n- EmrPregnancy, EmrPregnancyPlan, EmrEstimatedDueDate, EmrMultiBirth\n- EmrObUltrasound\n\n**Surgical:**\n- EmrSurgery, EmrSurghis (surgical history)\n- EmrDvtRisk (DVT risk assessment)\n\n**Vitals & Measurements:**\n- EmrMeasurement (~45 fields — vital signs, anthropometric data)\n\n**Lab Orders:**\n- EmrLabOrder\n\n**Documents & Images:**\n- Document (~60 fields — comprehensive document metadata including MIME types, categories, patient portal release, fax tracking)\n- EmrChartDocument\n\n**Patient Portal & Communication:**\n- PatMail (patient messaging)\n- SmsnaviConsent, SmsnaviMessages, SmsNaviNotification (SMS communications)\n- PatientSurvey, KioskAnswer, KioskPregOutcomeAnswer (patient-entered data)\n- PatientRequestAmendment, PatientRequestCallback, PatientRequestForm, PatientRequestOnline, PatientRequestRecall\n\n**Care Plans & Wellness:**\n- EmrWellnessPlan\n- EmrDisclosureInfo\n\n**Consent & Transfers:**\n- ConsentFormCompleted\n- EmrTransfer\n\n**Tasks:**\n- task, TaskAssigned\n\n**Access Control:**\n- EmrRestrictRecordAllow (restricted record permissions)\n- EmrEncounterProvider\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is an exceptionally thorough EHI export. The data dictionary documents **106 distinct data tables** covering virtually every data domain identified in the product research. This is a genuine (b)(10) export — not a FHIR/USCDI repackaging.\n\n**Clearly covered:**\n- Patient demographics and registration (extensive — ~170 fields in the Patients table alone)\n- Clinical documentation (chart notes, encounter reports, HPI, assessments, plans)\n- Problems/diagnoses with ICD codes\n- Medications (via NewCrop integration)\n- Allergies (via NewCrop)\n- Lab orders\n- Vital signs and measurements\n- Immunizations (with full vaccine administration details)\n- Appointments and scheduling\n- **Billing and financial data** — Procedure, ProcedureCharge, LedgerItem, Payment, Insurance, PriorAuth. This is a critical domain that many vendors miss.\n- **IVF/Fertility-specific data** — This is where nAbleMD's specialty focus really shows. The export includes ~25+ IVF-specific tables covering cycles, oocytes, semen analysis, follicular ultrasound, donor records, cryostorage billing, embryology worklists, culture media, and more. This is exactly the kind of specialty-specific clinical data that distinguishes a real (b)(10) export.\n- **OB/GYN data** — pregnancy history, OB ultrasound, estimated due dates, birth records\n- Documents and images (with repository of actual files)\n- Patient portal communications and messaging\n- SMS communications\n- Consent forms\n- Surgical history\n- Care plans and wellness plans\n- Patient surveys and kiosk-entered data\n- Referrals and transfers\n- EDI/claims data (835, 837, 277 messages in the document repository)\n\n**Potentially missing or unclear:**\n- **e-Prescribing transmission records** — NewcropDrug covers medication data, but transmission/fill status details are unclear. The NewCrop integration likely handles this on the NewCrop side.\n- **Clinical decision support data** — No dedicated CDS table, though CDS rules may be system configuration rather than patient data.\n- **Quality measure data** — No explicit CQM results table, though the underlying clinical data that feeds CQMs is present.\n- **Explicit radiology/imaging results** — EmrLabOrder covers lab orders but there's no dedicated radiology report table. DICOM files are included in the document repository and imaging results may be stored as documents.\n\nThese gaps are minor. The export comprehensively covers the designated record set.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **proprietary CSV-based format** — not FHIR, not C-CDA, not any standardized healthcare interchange format. This is actually appropriate for a (b)(10) export of this scope:\n\n- **CSV is universal.** Any system can read it. No FHIR parsing libraries required.\n- **The relational structure is preserved.** Tables reference each other via key fields (patientkey, visitkey, etc.), maintaining the database's relational integrity.\n- **Binary data is included.** The document repository preserves original file formats (PDF, DICOM, HL7, images, EDI messages) rather than trying to force everything into a text format.\n- **The format matches the data model.** Unlike trying to squeeze 106 tables into FHIR resources (many of which have no FHIR equivalent — EmrOocyteDay? CryoBilling? EmrCycleDrugPlan?), the CSV export simply mirrors the database schema.\n\nA third party could reconstruct a reasonably complete patient record from this export, given the data dictionary documentation. The key relationships (patientkey → other tables) are documented. The main limitation is that relationships are documented implicitly through key name matching rather than an explicit schema definition.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- The data dictionary is comprehensive — 106 tables, each with field-level descriptions\n- Export process instructions are clear and specific (which screens, which buttons, in what order)\n- Format documentation explains CSV encoding, ZIP encryption, and document repository structure\n- The Google Sheets format makes it easy to navigate between tables\n- Field descriptions are meaningful — not just column names repeated, but actual explanations of what the data represents\n- Revision history is maintained (though only 2 entries so far)\n- The Table of Contents provides a quick index\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **No explicit data types.** Fields are described in prose but there's no column for \"string\", \"integer\", \"date\", \"boolean\", etc. You can usually infer types from descriptions (\"Date when...\" = date, \"Indicates if...\" = boolean), but a developer would need to examine actual export data to confirm.\n- **No value set enumerations.** Coded fields (like gender, marital status, place of service) mention codes in passing within descriptions but don't provide exhaustive value set lists.\n- **No cardinality or constraint documentation.** Which fields are required? What's the max length of string fields? Not specified.\n- **No sample data or worked examples.** A sample export file would help developers understand the actual format.\n- **No explicit foreign key documentation.** Key relationships are mentioned in descriptions (e.g., \"Map with patientkey\") but there's no formal entity-relationship diagram or schema definition.\n- **The XLSX export doesn't work** — the Google Sheets direct export endpoint requires authentication, so the spreadsheet can only be accessed via browser or the gviz CSV endpoint. This could be an accessibility concern for some users.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity:** Field-level documentation for every column in every exported table. This is more granular than many vendors provide.\n\n**Breadth:** 106 data tables covering every major data domain. The IVF/fertility tables are remarkably detailed — the EmrCycle table alone has ~200+ fields documenting every aspect of an IVF treatment cycle. This is specialty-specific clinical data that most EHR vendors would never think to include in an EHI export.\n\n**The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) distinction:** nAbleMD gets this right. The EHI export section is separate from the FHIR API documentation section on the certification page. The export is a bulk CSV dump of the entire database, not a FHIR endpoint. The data dictionary documents tables that have no FHIR equivalent — this is genuine (b)(10) work, not (g)(10) relabeled.\n\n**Notable disclosure:** The certification page explicitly states that \"photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries\" and that \"a one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation.\" This means the standard export covers structured data, while binary content requires an additional fee. The document repository is described in the data dictionary documentation, so the capability exists — it's just priced separately.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nThis is one of the more thorough EHI export implementations encountered. Nth Technologies has done genuine (b)(10) work:\n\n1. **They built a real export mechanism** — not just a FHIR endpoint relabeled, but a purpose-built CSV bulk export with encryption, volume splitting, and document repository support.\n2. **They documented it comprehensively** — 106 tables with field-level descriptions in a well-organized Google Sheets workbook.\n3. **They include specialty-specific data** — the extensive IVF/fertility tables demonstrate that they're exporting data that goes far beyond USCDI/US Core.\n4. **They include billing data** — Procedure, Payment, Insurance, LedgerItem, PriorAuth — a critical domain many vendors omit.\n5. **They include documents** — the document repository handles PDFs, DICOM, HL7, EDI, images, and faxes.\n\nThe documentation could be improved with explicit data types, value sets, sample data, and an ERD. But the substance is strong. A developer receiving this export and data dictionary would have a reasonable chance of importing the data into another system — which is the fundamental purpose of (b)(10).\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (page is static HTML; Google Sheet requires gviz endpoint workaround for CSV download)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (EHI section is a single link on the certification page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none for the main page; Google Sheets direct XLSX export requires authentication but gviz CSV endpoint works without it\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The Google Sheets XLSX export endpoint (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/.../export?format=xlsx) returns an HTML auth wall rather than the file. The gviz/tq CSV endpoint works fine as an alternative.\n- Getting all 109 sheet GIDs required fetching the htmlview version of the spreadsheet and parsing the JavaScript initialization code for gid-to-name mappings. The edit view doesn't update the URL hash when clicking tabs in read-only mode.\n- No issues accessing the main certification page (standard Apache server, no WAF/Cloudflare).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1847,"cache_read_input_tokens":111142,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1847},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3a2a27aa-0d8e-4d83-820c-9d922f391773","uuid":"30b1d745-077c-4a7c-bc21-0f452671f74b"}

The direct XLSX export endpoint returned HTML auth walls, so per-sheet CSV via the gviz endpoint was used instead.\n\n6. **Noted important context from the \"Costs and Requirements\" section** on the certification page:\n   > \"While this product-version is certified for Data Portability to generate a set of export summaries of all patients; photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries. A one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation.\"\n\n   This indicates that the standard export covers structured data, while binary documents/images require a separate fee-based bulk export.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### Export Mechanism\n\nThe nAbleMD EHI export is a **CSV-based bulk export** with an accompanying document repository. The export produces an encrypted 7-zip archive containing:\n\n1. **CSV files** — one per data table (106+ tables), with UTF-8 encoding, comma-separated, first row as headers\n2. **A document repository folder** — containing scanned documents, DICOM files, HL7 messages, faxes, and other attachments referenced by the Document CSV table\n\n### How to Perform the Export\n\nPer the \"Read Me\" tab:\n- **Authorization**: An administrator must grant the user access to the Data Export screen under System Configuration. The user must also enable 2FA on their account.\n- **Single patient export**: PM Home → System Configuration → Data Export → select patient → \"Request Download\" → enter encryption password. Takes ~5 minutes per patient.\n- **Full export**: Same screen, but click \"Request Download\" without selecting a patient. Duration depends on total data volume.\n- **Retrieval**: Completed exports show checksums and download links. Each zip volume is ~10GB. Files retained for 7 days.\n\n### Export Format Details\n\n- **Archive format**: 7-zip with AES-256 encryption, split into ~10GB volumes (.zip.001, .zip.002, etc.)\n- **CSV format**: Standard CSV with UTF-8 encoding. No distinction between empty string and NULL. Strings containing commas, newlines, or quotes are enclosed in double quotes with standard escaping.\n- **Document repository**: Files referenced by the Document table's filename column. Includes:\n  - Documents/images: .pdf, .png, .jpg, .gif, .tif, .doc, .docx\n  - ANSI claim/EDI messages: .835, .837, .277, .277FE, .271, .271.xml, .DPR, .EBR\n  - HL7 messages: .hl7 (.orm.hl7 for results, .oru.hl7 for orders)\n  - DICOM: .dcm (image or Structured Report data)\n\n### Data Dictionary Structure\n\nEach of the 106 data table tabs follows a consistent format:\n- **Table Description** — 1-2 sentences describing the table's purpose and primary key\n- **FieldName / Description** — two-column listing of every exported field with plain-English descriptions\n\nField descriptions include data types implicitly (dates described as \"Date when...\", boolean fields as \"Indicates if/whether...\", foreign keys identified as \"identifier for...\" or \"Map with patientkey\"). No explicit data types, constraints, or value set enumerations are provided, though some descriptions note format details (e.g., \"comma separated if multiple\", gender codes \"M:Male F:Female U:Unknown X:Undifferentiated Blank:Undocumented\").\n\n### Data Tables (106 tables organized by domain)\n\n**Patient Demographics & Registration:**\n- Patients (extensive — ~170 fields covering demographics, addresses, contacts, insurance, fertility-specific fields like blood type, Rh factor, partner info, custom fields 1-10)\n- PatientContact, PatientAllowedContacts, PatientGlobal, PatientNote, Relative, EmrBiologicalFamily\n\n**Clinical Documentation:**\n- ChartNote (chart notes with form content, signatures, cosigning, patient portal release)\n- CosignNote, EmrNotes, EmrEncounterReport, EmrEncounterReportAddendum\n- EmrHpi (History of Present Illness)\n- EmrChiefComplaint\n- EmrReviews (Review of Systems)\n- EmrAssessment\n- EmrPlan\n- EmrChecklistItem\n- EmrAnswerDetail\n\n**Encounters & Visits:**\n- Visit (~75 fields including ICD codes 1-12, claim ID, place of service, provider, charting/approval status)\n- Appointment, AppointmentWaitlist, Action\n\n**Problems, Medications & Allergies:**\n- EmrProblem (diagnoses/problems with ICD codes, onset dates, status)\n- EmrVisitProblem (visit-specific problems)\n- NewcropDrug (medications via NewCrop integration — ~50 fields)\n- NewcropAllergy (allergies via NewCrop)\n- EmrHealthConcern\n- EmrMedicalHistory\n\n**Billing & Financial:**\n- Procedure (CPT/HCPCS codes, modifiers, fees)\n- ProcedureCharge\n- LedgerItem\n- Payment, VisitPayment, PrePayment\n- Insurance (~80 fields — subscriber info, group numbers, authorization details)\n- PriorAuth (prior authorizations)\n- CryoBilling (IVF-specific billing)\n- IvfQuote (IVF treatment quotes)\n\n**Immunizations:**\n- ImmunizationRecord (~35 fields — vaccine codes, lot numbers, manufacturer, VIS dates, administration details)\n- ImmunizationSchedule\n\n**IVF/Fertility-Specific (extensive):**\n- EmrCycle (~200+ fields — comprehensive IVF cycle data)\n- EmrCycleHistory, EmrCycleIntents, EmrCycleDrugPlan, EmrCycleScheduleDay, EmrCycleScheduleRow, EmrCycleScheduleAlert\n- EmrCycleNote, EmrCycleEducation, EmrCycleBirth, EmrCycleCulture\n- EmrOocyte, EmrOocyteDay (oocyte tracking)\n- EmrIvfSample (specimen/sample tracking)\n- EmrIvfSemenAnalysis (~75 fields)\n- EmrIvfFollicularUs (follicular ultrasound)\n- EmrIvfObUs (OB ultrasound)\n- EmrSemenMeasurement\n- EmrDonor (~70 fields), DonorEducation, DonorEmployment, DonorFamily, DonorFamilyDeceased, DonorAnswer\n- EmrDonorPatrequest, CultureMedia\n- EmrInfertilityTreatment, CycleTypeHistory\n- DailyWorklist (embryology daily tasks)\n- EmrContraception\n\n**OB/GYN:**\n- EmrObHistory, EmrObHistoryPreg, EmrObgynhc\n- EmrPregnancy, EmrPregnancyPlan, EmrEstimatedDueDate, EmrMultiBirth\n- EmrObUltrasound\n\n**Surgical:**\n- EmrSurgery, EmrSurghis (surgical history)\n- EmrDvtRisk (DVT risk assessment)\n\n**Vitals & Measurements:**\n- EmrMeasurement (~45 fields — vital signs, anthropometric data)\n\n**Lab Orders:**\n- EmrLabOrder\n\n**Documents & Images:**\n- Document (~60 fields — comprehensive document metadata including MIME types, categories, patient portal release, fax tracking)\n- EmrChartDocument\n\n**Patient Portal & Communication:**\n- PatMail (patient messaging)\n- SmsnaviConsent, SmsnaviMessages, SmsNaviNotification (SMS communications)\n- PatientSurvey, KioskAnswer, KioskPregOutcomeAnswer (patient-entered data)\n- PatientRequestAmendment, PatientRequestCallback, PatientRequestForm, PatientRequestOnline, PatientRequestRecall\n\n**Care Plans & Wellness:**\n- EmrWellnessPlan\n- EmrDisclosureInfo\n\n**Consent & Transfers:**\n- ConsentFormCompleted\n- EmrTransfer\n\n**Tasks:**\n- task, TaskAssigned\n\n**Access Control:**\n- EmrRestrictRecordAllow (restricted record permissions)\n- EmrEncounterProvider\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is an exceptionally thorough EHI export. The data dictionary documents **106 distinct data tables** covering virtually every data domain identified in the product research. This is a genuine (b)(10) export — not a FHIR/USCDI repackaging.\n\n**Clearly covered:**\n- Patient demographics and registration (extensive — ~170 fields in the Patients table alone)\n- Clinical documentation (chart notes, encounter reports, HPI, assessments, plans)\n- Problems/diagnoses with ICD codes\n- Medications (via NewCrop integration)\n- Allergies (via NewCrop)\n- Lab orders\n- Vital signs and measurements\n- Immunizations (with full vaccine administration details)\n- Appointments and scheduling\n- **Billing and financial data** — Procedure, ProcedureCharge, LedgerItem, Payment, Insurance, PriorAuth. This is a critical domain that many vendors miss.\n- **IVF/Fertility-specific data** — This is where nAbleMD's specialty focus really shows. The export includes ~25+ IVF-specific tables covering cycles, oocytes, semen analysis, follicular ultrasound, donor records, cryostorage billing, embryology worklists, culture media, and more. This is exactly the kind of specialty-specific clinical data that distinguishes a real (b)(10) export.\n- **OB/GYN data** — pregnancy history, OB ultrasound, estimated due dates, birth records\n- Documents and images (with repository of actual files)\n- Patient portal communications and messaging\n- SMS communications\n- Consent forms\n- Surgical history\n- Care plans and wellness plans\n- Patient surveys and kiosk-entered data\n- Referrals and transfers\n- EDI/claims data (835, 837, 277 messages in the document repository)\n\n**Potentially missing or unclear:**\n- **e-Prescribing transmission records** — NewcropDrug covers medication data, but transmission/fill status details are unclear. The NewCrop integration likely handles this on the NewCrop side.\n- **Clinical decision support data** — No dedicated CDS table, though CDS rules may be system configuration rather than patient data.\n- **Quality measure data** — No explicit CQM results table, though the underlying clinical data that feeds CQMs is present.\n- **Explicit radiology/imaging results** — EmrLabOrder covers lab orders but there's no dedicated radiology report table. DICOM files are included in the document repository and imaging results may be stored as documents.\n\nThese gaps are minor. The export comprehensively covers the designated record set.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **proprietary CSV-based format** — not FHIR, not C-CDA, not any standardized healthcare interchange format. This is actually appropriate for a (b)(10) export of this scope:\n\n- **CSV is universal.** Any system can read it. No FHIR parsing libraries required.\n- **The relational structure is preserved.** Tables reference each other via key fields (patientkey, visitkey, etc.), maintaining the database's relational integrity.\n- **Binary data is included.** The document repository preserves original file formats (PDF, DICOM, HL7, images, EDI messages) rather than trying to force everything into a text format.\n- **The format matches the data model.** Unlike trying to squeeze 106 tables into FHIR resources (many of which have no FHIR equivalent — EmrOocyteDay? CryoBilling? EmrCycleDrugPlan?), the CSV export simply mirrors the database schema.\n\nA third party could reconstruct a reasonably complete patient record from this export, given the data dictionary documentation. The key relationships (patientkey → other tables) are documented. The main limitation is that relationships are documented implicitly through key name matching rather than an explicit schema definition.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- The data dictionary is comprehensive — 106 tables, each with field-level descriptions\n- Export process instructions are clear and specific (which screens, which buttons, in what order)\n- Format documentation explains CSV encoding, ZIP encryption, and document repository structure\n- The Google Sheets format makes it easy to navigate between tables\n- Field descriptions are meaningful — not just column names repeated, but actual explanations of what the data represents\n- Revision history is maintained (though only 2 entries so far)\n- The Table of Contents provides a quick index\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **No explicit data types.** Fields are described in prose but there's no column for \"string\", \"integer\", \"date\", \"boolean\", etc. You can usually infer types from descriptions (\"Date when...\" = date, \"Indicates if...\" = boolean), but a developer would need to examine actual export data to confirm.\n- **No value set enumerations.** Coded fields (like gender, marital status, place of service) mention codes in passing within descriptions but don't provide exhaustive value set lists.\n- **No cardinality or constraint documentation.** Which fields are required? What's the max length of string fields? Not specified.\n- **No sample data or worked examples.** A sample export file would help developers understand the actual format.\n- **No explicit foreign key documentation.** Key relationships are mentioned in descriptions (e.g., \"Map with patientkey\") but there's no formal entity-relationship diagram or schema definition.\n- **The XLSX export doesn't work** — the Google Sheets direct export endpoint requires authentication, so the spreadsheet can only be accessed via browser or the gviz CSV endpoint. This could be an accessibility concern for some users.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity:** Field-level documentation for every column in every exported table. This is more granular than many vendors provide.\n\n**Breadth:** 106 data tables covering every major data domain. The IVF/fertility tables are remarkably detailed — the EmrCycle table alone has ~200+ fields documenting every aspect of an IVF treatment cycle. This is specialty-specific clinical data that most EHR vendors would never think to include in an EHI export.\n\n**The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) distinction:** nAbleMD gets this right. The EHI export section is separate from the FHIR API documentation section on the certification page. The export is a bulk CSV dump of the entire database, not a FHIR endpoint. The data dictionary documents tables that have no FHIR equivalent — this is genuine (b)(10) work, not (g)(10) relabeled.\n\n**Notable disclosure:** The certification page explicitly states that \"photographs, scanned images, faxes, other uploaded documents as well as medical documentation not included in the Common Data Set are not included in the export summaries\" and that \"a one-time fee will be charged for the bulk export of these images, documents and documentation.\" This means the standard export covers structured data, while binary content requires an additional fee. The document repository is described in the data dictionary documentation, so the capability exists — it's just priced separately.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nThis is one of the more thorough EHI export implementations encountered. Nth Technologies has done genuine (b)(10) work:\n\n1. **They built a real export mechanism** — not just a FHIR endpoint relabeled, but a purpose-built CSV bulk export with encryption, volume splitting, and document repository support.\n2. **They documented it comprehensively** — 106 tables with field-level descriptions in a well-organized Google Sheets workbook.\n3. **They include specialty-specific data** — the extensive IVF/fertility tables demonstrate that they're exporting data that goes far beyond USCDI/US Core.\n4. **They include billing data** — Procedure, Payment, Insurance, LedgerItem, PriorAuth — a critical domain many vendors omit.\n5. **They include documents** — the document repository handles PDFs, DICOM, HL7, EDI, images, and faxes.\n\nThe documentation could be improved with explicit data types, value sets, sample data, and an ERD. But the substance is strong. A developer receiving this export and data dictionary would have a reasonable chance of importing the data into another system — which is the fundamental purpose of (b)(10).\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.nablemd.com/certification2015.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (page is static HTML; Google Sheet requires gviz endpoint workaround for CSV download)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (EHI section is a single link on the certification page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none for the main page; Google Sheets direct XLSX export requires authentication but gviz CSV endpoint works without it\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The Google Sheets XLSX export endpoint (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/.../export?format=xlsx) returns an HTML auth wall rather than the file. The gviz/tq CSV endpoint works fine as an alternative.\n- Getting all 109 sheet GIDs required fetching the htmlview version of the spreadsheet and parsing the JavaScript initialization code for gid-to-name mappings. The edit view doesn't update the URL hash when clicking tabs in read-only mode.\n- No issues accessing the main certification page (standard Apache server, no WAF/Cloudflare).\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}

(nAbleMD)** — EHI export documentation successfully downloaded.\n\n**What was found:**\n- The registered URL is a certification/mandatory disclosures page with a dedicated \"Electronic Health Information Export\" section linking to a Google Sheets data dictionary\n- The data dictionary (\"CSV Export Format Documentation - External\") contains **109 tabs** documenting **106 data tables** plus a Read Me, Revision History, and Table of Contents\n- All 109 sheets were downloaded as CSV files (the XLSX export endpoint was blocked, but the gviz/tq endpoint worked)\n\n**Key findings:**\n- This is a **genuine (b)(10) export** — CSV-based bulk export of the full database, not a FHIR endpoint relabeled\n- **106 data tables** covering demographics, clinical notes, problems, medications, allergies, vitals, immunizations, billing, insurance, documents, and extensive IVF/fertility-specific data (~25+ specialty tables)\n- Export produces an encrypted 7-zip archive with CSV files and a document repository (PDFs, DICOM, HL7, EDI, images)\n- The documentation is comprehensive at the field level but lacks explicit data types, value sets, and sample data\n- Binary documents/images require a separate one-time fee for bulk export\n\n**Output files:**\n- `ehi-export-report.md` — detailed narrative report with coverage assessment\n- `files.json` — manifest of 113 downloaded files\n- `downloads/` — 3 screenshots, 1 HTML page, 109 CSV data dictionary files"}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":236,"cache_read_input_tokens":121155,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":236},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3a2a27aa-0d8e-4d83-820c-9d922f391773","uuid":"5020cf4f-44a5-43bb-a630-40f9f77056e3"}
